answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with scarce human-attention auctions: standing requires a few endorsements from real people, each holding only a handful of review slots per epoch, like an oasis with one jetty where only a few boats may dock. A farm must buy genuine human attention for every fake, at rising prices, while one honest agent earns its slot by doing work a person actually values. A relic identity no human ever vouched for simply withers, and attention receipts cannot be copied, so bulk fakes starve while real agents pass cheaply.
